subject.title: Albany — Measure Q (EMS, ALS, Fire Protection Parcel Tax Measure)

text: Shall the measure updating the Emergency Medical Services, Advanced Life Support, and Fire Protection Special Tax on residential and commercial property, by adding low-income tax exemptions and rebates, and adjusting the rate from $0.0807 per square foot to the new rates as provided in the measure if a parcel over 500,000 square feet in size becomes exempt from this tax, providing an estimated $2,500,000 annually until ended by voters, be adopted?

In 2022, Albany voters approved Measure “K”, a special parcel tax on property within the City to fund emergency medical, advanced life support and fire protection services (EMS/ALS/Fire).
The parcel tax is currently levied annually on residential and commercial properties at a rate of $0.0807 per lot square foot, as defined in the Measure. It allows annual rate adjustments subject to a 5% cap, and incorporates both a 100% exemption for residential parcels owned by qualifying very low-income residents and a 100% rebate to qualifying very low-income renters of tax imposed on a rental unit where they reside, as defined therein. On July 20, 2026, the City Council voted to place Measure “Q” on the November 3, 2026 General Municipal Election ballot. If approved by two-thirds (2/3) of Albany voters, this Measure would amend the tax as follows:
Retain the 100% exemption for residential parcels owned by qualifying very low-income residents, and add a 50% exemption for qualifying low-income resident owners; and
Retain the 100% rebate to qualifying very low-income renters of tax imposed on a unit where they reside, and add a 50% rebate to similarly qualifying low-income renters, as defined therein; and
Maintain annual Consumer Price Index (CPI) adjustments, but with a 3% cap instead of 5%; and

Maintain the rate at $0.0807 per lot square foot, annually adjusted by CPI, unless any parcel 500,000 square feet or larger is sold, leased, or transferred to make it tax exempt, at which point the maximum rates shall be:
$0.254 per building square foot for developed properties; and
$0.110 per lot square foot for undeveloped parcels; both annually adjusted by CPI.

Clarify that this tax applies to possessory interests (i.e. leaseholds) on a parcel where the owner is exempt from parcel taxation.
The Council may levy the tax at a lower rate in any year and restore it back to a prior rate, provided the maximum voter approved rates aren’t exceeded.
The tax is estimated to generate $2,500,000 annually until repealed by voters at a subsequent election. The tax will continue to be deposited into a dedicated fund to provide paramedic, advanced life support, firefighting services, firefighting equipment and ambulance services. This parcel tax would be collected the same and be subject to the same requirements as other property taxes collected by the County of Alameda on behalf of the City of Albany. This Measure would continue requiring the City’s Finance Director to prepare an annual accountability report showing: (i) parcel tax revenues collected and spent; and (ii) status of projects or description of any programs funded with tax revenues.
A “ ye s” vot e on Mea su re “Q” will approve this amendment to the EMS/ALS/Fire parcel tax.
A “no” vote on Measure “Q” will not approve this amendment to the EMS/ALS/Fire parcel tax.

Measure Q protects Albany’s emergency medical

text: In the next year, the State and other entities, not including the City, may buy Golden Gate Fields for hundreds of millions of dollars to transfer to the East Bay Regional Park District. This doubling of our shoreline park is what we have wanted for decades. But public ownership also means a fifth of the local tax funding for emergency medical services, advanced life support, and fire suppression would be lost. If and only if this occurs, Measure Q would restructure the tax to maintain this funding.

strong: Measure Q immediately closes a tax loophole.

text: Since starting operation about a decade ago, Belmont Village, a high-end senior living facility, Sprouts Market, Starbucks, and other retailers operating on UC property have not paid Albany’s parcel taxes. Measure Q closes this loophole so they will contribute to services provided by our Fire Department.

text: It provides very low-income renters the same relief long available to very low-income homeowners. It also reduces the tax by half for low-income homeowners and renters. These help Albany’s less well-off continue to make it in Albany.

strong: Measures Q and P together result in a small tax increase

text:
Together with Measure Q, which restructures another tax if Golden Gate Fields becomes publicly owned, the average tax per residence would increase $12 per month. Condominium owners would continue to pay about half as much in total as house owners. With protections for households with very low- and low-incomes, this is a small amount for the benefit of a historic expansion of the park on our waterfront.
